newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney 1995/96 profit jumps 77 pct.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney 1995/96 profit jumps 77 pct.

text.p: Euro Disney on Tuesday reported a 77 percent jump in profit for the 1995/96 year ended September 30 to 202 million francs, helped by a nine percent rise in attendance to its Disneyland Paris theme park to a record 11.7 million visitors.
"We are proud of what has been accomplished in a difficult economic environment, particularly for the tourism industry," Euro Disney chairman Philippe Bourguignon said in a statement.
The results, marking the company's second annual profit, appear to confirm its recovery after a difficult start in 1992.
After losing more than seven billion francs in its first two years, Euro Disney posted a net profit of 114 million francs in 1994/95.
Income excluding exceptional items for the year to September 30, 1996, rose to 156 million francs from two million in the previous year.

But Bourguignon cautioned that the coming year posed a challenge. "Persistent weakness in the economy, constant pressure on our prices, and the strong increase in financial charges constitute several real challenges for the future, particularly in 1997," he said.
"One thing is certain: our public endorsement is definitely demonstrated," he said.
Euro Disney is 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co.
